messages:
evan-sales: FYI ACME wants finalized numbers for reserved GPU commit + autoscale policy by EOD. They sent a traffic dump.
alice-se: cool — paste the important bits here or attach link
evan-sales: attaching summary: steady 220 RPS gen, daily peak bursts up to 1.9k RPS for ~8-12min, avg 320 tokens/gen, 20% streaming, 15% embeddings (lower compute). 95th op latency target 300ms.
carla-se: thanks. Are those single-model or mixed-model traffic? batching behavior matters a lot.
evan-sales: mixed. 70% on a chat model (longer context ~2k tokens), 15% rerank, 15% embeddings. Burst pattern: sudden fanout from webhook -> 2–3x concurrency spike then gradual tail.
ben-fin: quick pricing question — customer prefers a monthly reserved commit with burst credits. Need recommended baseline GPUs + burst cap to produce an ARR estimate.
maria-ps: also flag: ACME's sec questionnaire asks about node isolation and private keys for KMS — will coordinate with security but that doesn't change sizing.
carla-se: rough back-of-envelope: if we serve quantized chat (8-bit) with batching and KV cache hit ~40%, each A100-equivalent can handle ~220 steady RPS gen (mix), but burst efficiency drops. For their peak of 1.9k, we need ~9–10 GPUs warm. For safety and headroom I'd recommend baseline 12 reserved, burst to 36 using burst credits/spot nodes + 3s batching window.
alice-se: 12 baseline seems low given 2k peak — rationale pls (want to avoid underprovisioning during business hour spikes)
carla-se: rationale: steady 220 RPS matches one node if token distribution centralized. We assume aggressive batching (20–30ms queue) and prefix caching. But because 20% streaming bypasses batching, add 30% headroom. That's how we get to 12. If they insist on 99th latency SLO under 300ms, add another 4 nodes.
evan-sales: can you show an autoscale policy snippet we can propose? customer wants deterministic preheat window.
carla-se: sure. paste this into the proposal:

```
{
  "policy": "target_utilization",
  "target": 0.6,
  "scale_up": { "step": 4, "min_cooldown_s": 180 },
  "scale_down": { "step": 2, "min_cooldown_s": 300 },
  "preheat": { "enabled": true, "window_s": 600, "min_warm_nodes": 12 },
  "burst_pool": { "enabled": true, "max_nodes": 36, "spot_fallback": true }
}
```

carla-se: notes: preheat window 600s (10m) to allow model weights to warm and KV cache to prime; scale_up step 4 to avoid small frequent increments during spikes.
ben-fin: for pricing I need baseline: 16 reserved GPUs @ committed rate, plus ability to burst to 36 (pay-as-you-go for extras). Is 16 defensible?
carla-se: yes — if ACME wants p99 latency guarantees, recommend 16 baseline. If they accept p95, 12 baseline + autoscale works and reduces commit cost.
alice-se: what about AZ affinity? customer requires multi-AZ for DR.
carla-se: recommend split baseline across 2 AZs (8/8) with cross-AZ fallback. Keep burst pool able to allocate in either AZ depending on capacity.
maria-ps: security ask: will preheating leak data across customers if we reuse nodes? we need to confirm node tenancy model in the proposal.
carla-se: for Dedicated customers we provide tenant-isolated GPU pools. Preheat uses their isolated pool only — add sentence to proposal to reassure.
evan-sales: thanks. I'll draft the commit options: Option A (p95 SLA): 12 reserved, burst to 36, est monthly commit $X (need ben). Option B (p99 SLA): 16 reserved, burst 36, higher commit.
ben-fin: I'll run numbers. prelim estimate: commit price for 16 reserved (quantized workloads) is ~25% discount off on-demand; will send calc in 90m.
deploy-bot: Reserve request created: req-55321 for 12 -> 36 burst pool (pending finance approval)
alice-se: next steps — add these two options into the PO (include autoscale JSON), get security confirmation on KMS + isolation, finance to confirm pricing, then final sign-off call tomorrow 10am PT.
evan-sales: copying customer success and legal. I'll update ACME with Option A+B and schedule 10am PT call.
ben-fin: uploaded initial pricing spreadsheet to drive: https://redwood.drive/ACME/commit-pricing
carla-se: I'll also include quantization recommendations and a perf test runbook (5–10 min smoke with 2k RPS spikes) in the annex.
alice-se: perfect. done here unless someone flags a risk.
maria-ps: one more — security will require an encrypted audit log for preheat operations. tagging @security for quick confirm.
evan-sales: thanks team :thumbsup:
